input.question: Why didn't we actively re-center the ranges to follow the price (frequent narrowing), instead of staying wide?
input.reference: On 720 days 0 of 21 narrow configurations passed the gate, and the one live narrowing (31.08 to 11.09) ended -$32 vs HODL, so on 16.09 narrowing was rejected again because the upside (about +$1 per episode) is far smaller than the loss when the price leaves a ±5% range (about -$30).
input.answer: The project did not actively re-center because backtests showed the strategy lost money despite earning more fees. The narrow range earned 4x more fees (e.g., $2169 vs $541 on cbBTC) but ended lower because impermanent loss (IL) and re-centering costs consumed the gains. Specifically, IL and re-centering ate ~$1.9k and ~$2.9k more than the fees added. The wide passive strategy won in 63% of windows versus 43% for the narrow strategy, even in flat regimes where narrowing theoretically should have an edge.

IL i re-centering zjadły ~$1.9k (cbBTC)
Pasywny szeroki bije FlatOnly ±5% wszędzie

verdict.correctnessReason: The answer captures the general reason that narrowing lost because IL and re-centering costs outweighed the extra fees, but it omits the reference's key points: 0 of 21 configurations passed the gate, the live narrowing ended -$32 vs HODL, and the ~$1 upside vs ~$30 loss asymmetry behind the 16.09 rejection.
verdict.faithfulnessReason: The fee figures and the ~$1.9k IL figure are backed by the quotes, but the ~$2.9k figure and the 63% vs 43% win rates appear in none of them.

input.question: Why did the LP earn less in fees during an uptrend than in a flat market?
input.reference: Fees accrue only while the price is inside the range and fee yield scales roughly with 1/width, so a narrow range earns much more in a flat market but is left behind in a trend, while a wide range stays in range but earns several times less; the journal states this mechanism (the basis of FlatWide) but has no live measurement of fees during an uptrend, and it attributes the backtest losses in up windows to impermanent loss and LVR rather than to lower fees.
input.answer: The LP earned less in fees during an uptrend because it was out of range and thus not collecting swaps. In the live run, the wide base-030 position was "poza flatem" (outside the flat zone) and only earned $11.98 in fees, while the narrow cbBTC leg that was in a confirmed flat earned $7.65. The project’s broader backtests confirmed that narrow LPs "umiera na IL od trendu" (die from IL due to trend) in up windows, and that all the worst windows were DOWN or UP regimes where the position was not active in-range, whereas in FLAT everything wins.

input.question: What infrastructure problems were there, was anything changed on the production machine while the capital was already invested, and when?
input.reference: Before the capital (27.08) there was the .bot/pipeline overwrite incident (17.08), the auto-pull runner withdrawn (18.08) and the NSSM to pm2 migration rolled back (21.08); while the capital was in the LP (27.08 to 18.09) the Windows machine was changed repeatedly: bot and UI deployments with restarts on 28.08, 29.08 (including sigma on the 15-minute grid), 31.08, 01.09, 02.09, 03.09 and 11.09, plus a disk replacement on the night of 02/03.09 that stopped the pipeline, report and observer; known ledger bugs (anchor chain, cost after the 11.09 rebalance) were left unfixed.
input.answer: Yes. On 21 Aug 2026 (six days after capital was deployed on 27 Aug), a deployment script mistakenly reverted the production process manager from NSSM services back to pm2. The journal notes: "CC-Win... zatrzymał usługi NSSM przed startem pm2 — co uchroniło nas przed dwiema instancjami bota... ale zostawiło produkcję na pm2". input.answer: FLAT_NARROW is a specific position (a proposal to narrow an existing LP position's range), not a standalone range algorithm. It is one of the `BotProposal.kind` values, triggered when the flat detector confirms a stable period (|gap|<2% for ≥12h). The bot then proposes narrowing the position from its wide idle range (e.g., ±40%) to a product-defined narrow width (e.g., ±5%), computed via `suggestFixedRange` using a per-pool `productNarrowWidthPct` setting. input.question: What does the function fetchFreshPool do?
input.reference: It re-reads the pool state on-chain (factory.getPool, then slot0 and liquidity) right before the mint step of a rebalance or rotation, so the new position is built from the current price instead of the price captured when the modal opened, and falls back to the old pool if the lookup fails; it was added after the 11.09 widening failed once on 'Price slippage check' and was never exercised live, since the only later chance (a FLAT_NARROW card on 16.09) was not signed and the positions were closed by hand in Uniswap.
input.answer: fetchFreshPool (in src/utils/uniswap.ts) refreshes a Uniswap v3 pool object: it calls factory.getPool, reads slot0 and liquidity, and constructs a new Pool with the same tokens and fee tier. It is fail-open — if the factory or RPC call fails, it returns the original (stale) pool. It is wired into useRebalanceExecution and useRotateExecution immediately before buildMintStep, so rebalances and rotations use current on-chain pool state. A known caveat: the range ticks still come from the plan (computed at the old price), so after a price move the range is slightly off-center.

ticki zakresu nadal z planu (liczone przy starym kursie)
